title: How Alex West got to CyberLeads after 19 failed products: build boring, double down
summary: Alex West explains how 19 failed products led to CyberLeads, a lead-gen newsletter for agencies. Lessons: build boring ideas people already pay for, learn from doing, find one product plus one distribution channel and double down, and treat competition as no threat. Also covers habits over motivation and why small teams can outmove companies.

principles.text: Build boring products people already pay for, not unique world-changing ones.
principles.quote: let's build something boring let's build something that i know that people will pay for let's build something without code

principles.text: Find an idea already validated by many players selling the same info to different audiences.
principles.quote: i found around 10 companies basically providing the same information to two different kinds of people and they're all making a lot of money

principles.text: Launch minimal: a landing page and a Gumroad subscription are enough to validate.
principles.quote: all i need is a landing page on a gumroad subscription i didn't even code like the the stripe checkout or something

principles.text: You need both a product and a distribution channel; once something works, double down on that one thing.
principles.quote: you have one product and one distribution channel double down on those

principles.text: Don't fear competition: the internet is huge, and you can niche down so you aren't truly competing.
principles.quote: the internet is so big if you think that i don't know the internet can't handle you and one other player just you're crazy

principles.text: A solo hacker moves far faster than a company and can pivot in a day.
principles.quote: in the hacker can pivot in a day like i can start i i started like general b2b sales with cyberleads and then one day i was going through my customers
